01_history_overview.md.title: History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan

03_scholars_writers_historians.md.title: Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region

headingPath: History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan
chunks.text:
History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan > Ancient and early medieval background

The territory of present-day Uzbekistan has long connected settled oasis civilizations, steppe peoples, and long-distance trade routes. Samarkand, Bukhara, Khiva, Termez and other cities developed at different times as political, commercial, religious and intellectual centres.

Samarkand grew from the ancient settlement known as Afrasiab. UNESCO describes the historic city as a major crossroads of cultures with more than two and a half millennia of history.

headingPath: History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan
chunks.text:
History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan > Arab conquest and Islamic period

Arab armies entered Transoxiana in the 7th and 8th centuries, and Islam gradually became deeply rooted in the region. Bukhara later became one of the most important centres of Islamic scholarship in Central Asia.

headingPath: History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan
chunks.text:
History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan > Samanid period

The Samanids ruled much of Central Asia in the 9th and 10th centuries. Bukhara was one of the dynasty's major political and cultural centres and became famous for scholarship, literature and religious learning.

headingPath: History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan
chunks.text:
History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan > Mongol conquest

In 1220, Mongol forces under Chinggis Khan captured major cities including Bukhara and Samarkand. The conquest caused major destruction, but urban and cultural life later recovered.

headingPath: History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan
chunks.text:
History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan > Timurid period

In the late 14th century, Timur made Samarkand the capital of a powerful empire. The Timurid period became especially important for architecture, manuscript culture, astronomy, mathematics and the arts.

headingPath: History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan
chunks.text:
History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan > Later states

From the early 16th century, Shaybanid rulers established power in much of Transoxiana. In later centuries, the region included the Khanate of Khiva, the Emirate of Bukhara and the Khanate of Kokand.

headingPath: History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan
chunks.text:
History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan > Russian conquest

Russian forces captured Tashkent in 1865. The Khanate of Kokand was abolished in 1876, while Bukhara and Khiva continued for a time as protectorates under strong Russian influence.

headingPath: History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan
chunks.text:
History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan > Soviet period

The Uzbek Soviet Socialist Republic was created in 1924. Soviet rule transformed education, industry, agriculture, language policy and urban life. Cotton production expanded enormously, while large-scale irrigation contributed to the later environmental crisis of the Aral Sea.

headingPath: History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan
chunks.text:
History of the territory of present-day Uzbekistan > Independence

Uzbekistan became independent in 1991. Independence Day is celebrated on 1 September.

Timurid era > Amir Temur

Amir Temur, known in many Western sources as Timur or Tamerlane, was born in 1336 near Kesh, the area of modern Shahrisabz. He rose to power in Transoxiana and established Samarkand as the main capital of his empire.

Timur's empire stretched across large parts of Central Asia, Iran, Afghanistan, the Caucasus and neighbouring regions. His campaigns were often destructive, while his court also concentrated craftsmen, scholars and architects in Samarkand.

Timur died in 1405. The Gur-e Amir mausoleum in Samarkand became his burial place and one of the best-known monuments associated with the dynasty.

Timurid era > Samarkand under the Timurids

UNESCO identifies the 14th and 15th centuries as Samarkand's most significant period of development. Major monuments include Bibi-Khanum Mosque, Shah-i-Zinda, Gur-e Amir, Ulugh Beg's madrasa and Ulugh Beg's observatory.

Timurid era > Ulugh Beg

Ulugh Beg, a grandson of Timur, was a Timurid ruler and astronomer. He governed Samarkand and became famous for supporting mathematics and astronomy.

Ulugh Beg founded a major observatory in Samarkand in the 15th century. Astronomers working there produced highly accurate observations of stars and planetary motion for their time.

Ulugh Beg also built a madrasa on the Registan.

headingPath: Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region
chunks.text:
Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region

Important: many people below lived centuries before modern Uzbek national identity developed. It is more accurate to describe them by their city, dynasty, language or region than to call all of them "Uzbek."

headingPath: Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region
chunks.text:
Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region > Muhammad al-Khwarizmi

Muhammad al-Khwarizmi was a 9th-century mathematician and astronomer associated by name with Khwarazm. He worked in Baghdad at the Abbasid court's scholarly centre.

His mathematical writings helped transmit methods for calculation and algebra. The word "algorithm" ultimately derives from the Latinized form of his name, while "algebra" comes from the title of one of his best-known works.

headingPath: Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region
chunks.text:
Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region > Abu Rayhan al-Biruni

Abu Rayhan al-Biruni was born in 973 in the Khwarazm region. He became one of the great polymaths of the medieval Islamic world.

He wrote on astronomy, mathematics, geography, chronology, mineralogy and the cultures of India.

headingPath: Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region
chunks.text:
Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region > Ibn Sina / Avicenna

Ibn Sina, known in Latin Europe as Avicenna, was born in 980 near Bukhara. He became a philosopher, physician and scholar.

His "Canon of Medicine" became one of the most influential medical texts of the medieval period.

headingPath: Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region
chunks.text:
Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region > Imam al-Bukhari

Muhammad ibn Ismail al-Bukhari was born in Bukhara in the 9th century. He became one of the most famous scholars of hadith in Sunni Islam.

His collection commonly known as Sahih al-Bukhari is one of the most influential hadith compilations in Sunni scholarship.

headingPath: Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region
chunks.text:
Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region > Al-Tirmidhi

Muhammad al-Tirmidhi was a 9th-century hadith scholar associated with the area of Termez. His Jami al-Tirmidhi became one of the major hadith collections used in Sunni scholarship.

headingPath: Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region
chunks.text:
Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region > Narshakhi

Muhammad ibn Jafar al-Narshakhi was a 10th-century historian from the Bukhara region. He wrote an early history of Bukhara in Arabic.

The original Arabic text has not survived, but the work became famous through a Persian translation and later revisions.

headingPath: Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region
chunks.text:
Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region > Alisher Navoi

Alisher Navoi was born in Herat in 1441 and became one of the most influential literary figures of the Timurid world. He wrote extensively in Chagatai Turkic and Persian.

Navoi's prestige helped establish Chagatai as a major literary language. Modern Uzbek literary culture regards him as a foundational classical author.

headingPath: Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region
chunks.text:
Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region > Zahiriddin Muhammad Babur

Babur was born in Andijan in 1483 into the Timurid dynasty. He later founded the Mughal Empire in northern India in 1526.

Babur wrote the Baburnama in Chagatai Turkic. It contains observations about politics, warfare, geography, plants, cities, people and court life.

headingPath: Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region
chunks.text:
Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region > Abdulla Qodiriy

Abdulla Qodiriy was a major figure in early modern Uzbek prose. His novel "O'tkan kunlar" is widely regarded as one of the foundational works of the modern Uzbek novel.

He was executed during the Stalinist purges in 1938.

headingPath: Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region
chunks.text:
Scholars, writers and historians connected to the region > Cho'lpon

Abdulhamid Cho'lpon was an Uzbek poet, writer, translator and intellectual active in the early Soviet period.

He was also killed during the Stalinist purges in 1938.

Jadidism and modern reformers > What was Jadidism?

Jadidism was a reform movement among Muslims of the Russian Empire and Central Asia in the late 19th and early 20th centuries. Jadids argued that education and society needed renewal.

A central idea was the "new method" school. These schools used more systematic teaching methods and introduced subjects such as arithmetic, geography, history and natural science alongside religious education.

The Jadids were not a single unified political group. They included moderates, radicals, religious reformers, writers, teachers, journalists and later political activists.

Jadidism and modern reformers > Mahmudkhoja Behbudi

Mahmudkhoja Behbudi was one of the leading Jadid reformers in Turkestan. He worked as an educator, journalist, playwright and public intellectual.

Behbudi promoted new-method schools and wrote educational materials. He also published the journal Oyna ("Mirror").

His play "Padarkush" became one of the foundational works of modern Central Asian theatre and used drama to argue for education and social reform.

Jadidism and modern reformers > Abdurauf Fitrat

Abdurauf Fitrat was born in Bukhara around 1886. He became one of the most influential intellectuals of the Bukharan Jadid movement.

Fitrat wrote in Persian/Tajik and Turkic/Uzbek and worked across literature, education, journalism, scholarship and politics.

He was arrested during the Stalinist purges and executed in 1938.

Jadidism and modern reformers > Jadid press

Jadid newspapers and journals discussed education, social reform, economics, culture, religion and politics. Publications became important spaces for the emergence of modern Uzbek prose and journalism.

Jadidism and modern reformers > Repression

Many major Jadid intellectuals were later accused of nationalism or anti-Soviet activity. A large part of the generation was killed or silenced during the Stalinist purges of the 1930s.

Historic cities and architecture > Samarkand

Samarkand is one of Central Asia's oldest major cities. UNESCO describes it as a crossroads and melting pot of world cultures.

The ancient settlement of Afrasiab forms an archaeological part of the city's history. Major monuments include Registan Square, Bibi-Khanum Mosque, Shah-i-Zinda, Gur-e Amir and Ulugh Beg's Observatory.

Historic cities and architecture > Registan

Registan is the monumental square at the heart of historic Samarkand. Its famous ensemble contains three madrasas built at different times: Ulugh Beg Madrasa, Sher-Dor Madrasa and Tilla-Kari Madrasa.

Historic cities and architecture > Bukhara

Bukhara has more than two thousand years of history and was a major centre on the Silk Roads.

UNESCO describes its historic centre as one of the best-preserved examples of a medieval Central Asian Islamic city.

The Ismail Samani Mausoleum is one of Bukhara's most famous early monuments and an outstanding example of 10th-century architecture.

Historic cities and architecture > Khiva and Itchan Kala

Itchan Kala is the walled inner city of Khiva. UNESCO describes it as a fortified historic town with a history of more than two millennia.

The walled area contains madrasas, mosques, mausoleums, caravanserais, markets and traditional houses.

Historic cities and architecture > UNESCO heritage

Uzbekistan has UNESCO World Heritage properties including the historic centres of Bukhara and Shahrisabz, Itchan Kala, Samarkand – Crossroad of Cultures, and the Silk Roads: Zarafshan-Karakum Corridor.

Culture and social life > Mahalla

A mahalla is a neighbourhood community and social institution. In Uzbekistan, mahallas historically organized local community life and often centred on shared spaces such as a mosque, teahouse, school, pond or local meeting area.

Mahallas have played roles in mutual assistance, ceremonies, neighbourhood relations, craft organization and communication between residents and local authorities.

Culture and social life > Hospitality

Hospitality is an important social value in Uzbek culture. Guests are commonly offered tea and food, and formal meals often involve a strong sense of respect for elders and visitors.

Regional and family customs vary, so the AI should avoid presenting one household practice as universal across all Uzbekistan.

Culture and social life > Navruz

Navruz marks the spring new year around the March equinox and is celebrated across many countries and peoples. In Uzbekistan it is associated with family gatherings, public festivities, food, music and seasonal renewal.

Culture and social life > Palov

Palov is one of the best-known dishes of Uzbekistan. It is commonly prepared with rice, meat, vegetables, oil or fat, and spices, although recipes vary by region and family.

UNESCO notes that palov is served both as an everyday meal and at important social occasions, including weddings, celebrations, acts of hospitality and commemorative gatherings.

Music, dance and oral traditions > Shashmaqom

Shashmaqom is a classical musical tradition shared especially by Uzbekistan and Tajikistan. Its name means "six maqoms."

The tradition combines instrumental music and vocal performance and developed in urban cultural centres of Central Asia.

UNESCO inscribed Shashmaqom on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2008.

Music, dance and oral traditions > Askiya

Askiya is an Uzbek verbal art based on witty dialogue and improvisation. Two or more performers exchange humorous remarks around a theme.

Successful performers need strong command of language, quick reasoning, observation and improvisation. UNESCO inscribed Askiya in 2014.

Music, dance and oral traditions > Lazgi

Lazgi is a dance tradition associated with Khorezm. UNESCO describes its movements as expressing human creativity, nature, love, happiness and everyday life.

It was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List in 2019.

Music, dance and oral traditions > Bakhshi art

Bakhshi are epic singers and storytellers who perform narrative poetry, often with musical accompaniment. The art depends heavily on memory, improvisation, oral transmission and apprenticeship.

Bakhshi art from Uzbekistan was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List in 2021.

Uzbek language > Language family

Uzbek is a Turkic language. It belongs to the Karluk branch of the Turkic language family and is closely related historically and linguistically to Uyghur.

Uzbek language > Historical literary background

For centuries, Chagatai Turkic served as a major written literary language of Central Asia. Writers such as Alisher Navoi and Babur used Chagatai.

Modern Uzbek literature developed partly from this Chagatai literary heritage.

Uzbek language > Grammar

Uzbek is generally agglutinative: grammatical information is often added through sequences of suffixes.

A common basic word order is subject-object-verb, although real Uzbek sentences can vary for emphasis and style.

Uzbek does not have grammatical gender comparable to languages such as Russian, French or German.

Uzbek language > Vocabulary

Uzbek has a Turkic grammatical core but contains many loanwords from Persian, Arabic, Russian and, more recently, international English-based vocabulary.

Uzbek language > Writing systems

Uzbek has been written in several scripts during its history. Arabic script was historically important for Chagatai and earlier literary traditions.

A Latin-based alphabet was used from 1929 to 1940. During the Soviet period, Uzbek was then written mainly in Cyrillic.

Independent Uzbekistan adopted a Latin-based Uzbek alphabet by law in 1993. The law was revised in 1995 to the modern system with 26 letters and 3 letter combinations.

Cyrillic Uzbek remains widely readable and is still encountered in books, signs, media and everyday writing.

Uzbek language > Modern Latin alphabet features

Modern Uzbek Latin writing includes distinctive forms such as Oʻ/oʻ and Gʻ/gʻ, as well as the combinations Sh/sh, Ch/ch and Ng/ng.

Crafts, textiles and material culture > Atlas and adras

Atlas and adras are traditional ikat fabrics associated strongly with Central Asian textile culture. Margilan became one of the most famous centres of production in present-day Uzbekistan.

In 2017, UNESCO selected the Margilan Crafts Development Centre's work safeguarding atlas and adras techniques for its Register of Good Safeguarding Practices.

Crafts, textiles and material culture > Suzani

Suzani is a traditional embroidered textile associated with settled communities in Central Asia, especially areas of present-day Uzbekistan and Tajikistan.

Historically, large suzanis were used to decorate interiors and were often part of a bride's dowry.

Crafts, textiles and material culture > Ceramics

Ceramic art is one of Uzbekistan's longstanding applied arts. Traditional pottery includes household vessels, jugs, storage containers, toys, architectural tiles and tandoor ovens.

Rishtan is especially famous for glazed ceramics and blue-green decorative traditions.

UNESCO inscribed Ceramic Arts in Uzbekistan on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2023.

Modern history and independence > Uzbek SSR

The Uzbek Soviet Socialist Republic was formed in 1924 during the Soviet national-territorial reorganization of Central Asia.

Samarkand served as the republic's capital in the 1920s before the capital was moved to Tashkent in 1930.

Modern history and independence > Soviet modernization

Soviet rule expanded mass education, industrialization, transportation and urban development. It also introduced strong state control over politics, religion, culture, agriculture and publishing.

Modern history and independence > Cotton and the Aral Sea

Uzbekistan became one of the Soviet Union's major cotton-producing regions. Extensive irrigation projects diverted water from the Amu Darya and Syr Darya systems.

The reduction of water reaching the Aral Sea contributed to one of the world's major environmental disasters.

Modern history and independence > Stalinist repression

During the 1930s, many Uzbek and Central Asian intellectuals, including prominent writers and Jadids, were arrested, imprisoned or executed during Stalinist purges.

Modern history and independence > Independence

In 1991, Uzbekistan became an independent state following the collapse of the Soviet Union. Independence Day is celebrated on 1 September.

Modern history and independence > Language after independence

After independence, Uzbekistan expanded the public role of Uzbek and adopted a Latin-based Uzbek alphabet by law in 1993, later revised in 1995.

headingPath: Ikki karra dengizga chiqish yo'li yo'q davlat
chunks.text:
Qiziqarli faktlar > Ikki karra dengizga chiqish yo'li yo'q davlat

O'zbekiston dunyodagi ikkita "ikki karra dengizga chiqish yo'li yo'q" (double-landlocked) davlatdan biri hisoblanadi. Bunday davlatga yetib borish uchun kamida ikkita davlat chegarasidan o'tish kerak. Ikkinchi bunday davlat — Lixtenshteyn.

Qiziqarli faktlar > Muruntau oltin koni

Muruntau koni Navoiy viloyatidagi Qizilqum cho'lida joylashgan bo'lib, ishlab chiqarish hajmi bo'yicha dunyodagi eng yirik oltin konlaridan biri hisoblanadi.

Qiziqarli faktlar > Usmon Qur'oni

Toshkentdagi Hazrati Imom majmuasida saqlanayotgan Usmon Qur'oni 8-9-asrlarga oid bo'lib, dunyodagi eng qadimiy Qur'on nusxalaridan biri hisoblanadi. U YUNESKOning "Jahon xotirasi" ro'yxatiga kiritilgan.

Qiziqarli faktlar > YUNESKO Jahon merosi ro'yxatidagi shaharlar

O'zbekistonda YUNESKO Jahon merosi ro'yxatiga kiritilgan to'rtta tarixiy shahar obidalari bor: Xivadagi Ichan qal'a 1990-yilda, Buxoro tarixiy markazi 1993-yilda, Shahrisabz tarixiy markazi 2000-yilda va Samarqand 2001-yilda ro'yxatga kiritilgan.

Qiziqarli faktlar > Teshiktash g'ori topilmasi

Teshiktash g'orida 1938-yilda neandertal bolasining qoldiqlari topilgan. Bu topilma taxminan 70 ming yil avvalgi davrga oid bo'lib, O'zbekiston hududida qadimgi odamlar yashaganini isbotlaydi.

Qiziqarli faktlar > Orol dengizining qurishi

Orol dengizi 1960-yillardan boshlab qishloq xo'jaligi uchun suv olinishi natijasida keskin qurib borgan. Mo'ynoq shahrida qurigan dengiz o'rnida "kemalar qabristoni" joylashgan bo'lib, u dunyodagi eng mashhur ekologik ogohlantirish ramzlaridan biriga aylangan.

Qiziqarli faktlar > Shashmaqom

Shashmaqom — Buxoroda shakllangan mumtoz musiqa janri bo'lib, olti maqomdan iborat. U YUNESKOning nomoddiy madaniy meros ro'yxatiga kiritilgan.

Qiziqarli faktlar > Palov (osh)

Palov (osh) o'zbek milliy taomi bo'lib, uni tayyorlash an'anasi YUNESKOning nomoddiy madaniy meros ro'yxatiga kiritilgan. O'zbekistonda palovning yuzdan ortiq turi mavjud.

Qiziqarli faktlar > Navro'z bayrami

Navro'z bayrami har yili 21-mart kuni nishonlanadi va bahor hamda yangi yil boshlanishini anglatadi. Navro'zda sumalak tayyorlash eng qadimiy an'analardan biri hisoblanadi. Sumalak undirilgan bug'doydan uzoq vaqt qaynatib tayyorlanadi.

Qiziqarli faktlar > Toshkent metropoliteni

Toshkent metropoliteni 1977-yilda ochilgan bo'lib, Markaziy Osiyodagi birinchi metro hisoblanadi. Uning bekatlari o'ziga xos me'moriy bezaklari bilan mashhur.

Qiziqarli faktlar > Samarqandning qadimiyligi

Samarqand dunyodagi eng qadimiy shaharlardan biri bo'lib, uning tarixi taxminan 2750 yildan ortiq davrni o'z ichiga oladi. Shahar Buyuk ipak yo'lining muhim markazi bo'lgan.

Qiziqarli faktlar > O'zbek tili

O'zbek tili turkiy tillar oilasiga mansub. O'zbekiston mustaqillikdan keyin lotin alifbosiga o'tish jarayonini boshlagan.

Temuriylar davri > Amir Temur > Tug'ilishi va saltanati

Amir Temur 1336-yilda Shahrisabz yaqinidagi Xo'ja Ilg'or qishlog'ida tug'ilgan. U 1370-yilda Movarounnahr hukmdori bo'ldi va Samarqandni o'z saltanatining poytaxti qildi. Amir Temur buyuk saltanat asoschisi bo'lib, uning davlati Markaziy Osiyodan Yaqin Sharqgacha cho'zilgan.

Temuriylar davri > Amir Temur > Anqara jangi

Amir Temur 1402-yilda Anqara jangida Usmonli sultoni Boyazid I ustidan g'alaba qozongan. Bu jang o'sha davrning eng yirik harbiy to'qnashuvlaridan biri edi.

Temuriylar davri > Amir Temur > Vafoti va Go'ri Amir maqbarasi

Amir Temur 1405-yilda Xitoyga yurish paytida O'tror shahrida vafot etgan. U Samarqanddagi Go'ri Amir maqbarasiga dafn etilgan. Go'ri Amir maqbarasi Temuriylar sulolasining muhim a'zolari dafn etilgan joy hisoblanadi.

Temuriylar davri > Bibixonim jome masjidi

Bibixonim jome masjidi Samarqandda 1399-1404 yillarda, Amir Temurning Hindiston yurishidan keyin qurilgan. U o'z davrida islom olamining eng katta masjidlaridan biri edi.

Temuriylar davri > Oqsaroy saroyi

Oqsaroy saroyi Shahrisabzda Amir Temur buyrug'i bilan qurilgan ulkan saroy bo'lgan. Uning peshtoqi qoldiqlari bugungi kungacha saqlanib qolgan.

Temuriylar davri > Mirzo Ulug'bek > Tug'ilishi va Samarqand hokimligi

Mirzo Ulug'bek 1394-yilda tug'ilgan bo'lib, Amir Temurning nabirasi edi. U 1409-yildan Samarqand hokimi bo'lgan va olim hukmdor sifatida tarixda qolgan.

Temuriylar davri > Mirzo Ulug'bek > Ulug'bek rasadxonasi

Mirzo Ulug'bek 1428-1429 yillarda Samarqandda mashhur rasadxona qurdirgan. Rasadxonaning asosiy asbobi ulkan sekstant bo'lgan. Ulug'bek rasadxonasida olib borilgan kuzatishlar asosida "Ziji jadidi Ko'ragoniy" asari yaratilgan bo'lib, unda 1018 yulduzning aniq jadvali keltirilgan.

Temuriylar davri > Mirzo Ulug'bek > Vafoti va ilmiy merosi

Mirzo Ulug'bek 1449-yilda fitna natijasida o'ldirilgan. Uning ilmiy merosi jahon astronomiyasi tarixida muhim o'rin tutadi.

Temuriylar davri > Registon maydoni

Registon maydoni Samarqandning markaziy maydoni bo'lib, uchta madrasadan iborat. Ulug'bek madrasasi 1417-1420 yillarda qurilgan. Sherdor madrasasi 1619-1636 yillarda, Tillakori madrasasi esa 1646-1660 yillarda qurilgan. Registon maydoni O'zbekistonning eng mashhur me'moriy yodgorliklaridan biri hisoblanadi.

Temuriylar davri > Zahiriddin Muhammad Bobur

Zahiriddin Muhammad Bobur Temuriylar avlodidan bo'lib, 1526-yilda Hindistonda Boburiylar imperiyasiga asos solgan. U "Boburnoma" nomli mashhur memuar asarining muallifidir.
